validity.researcher_notes: The Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Pipeline is a real, FERC-certificated facility (171 FERC P 61,134, docket CP17-178-000, issued 2020-05-21), independently corroborated by AGDC's own PTTL ROW-lease application and Resource Report No. 1. Classification as Gas/transmission is correct -- see the Fuel and PipelineType fills. Caveat: as of the 2026-04-01 DOE/FECM report, Phase One 'may also include' this lateral -- its inclusion is Glenfarne's stated intent, not yet locked in a construction contract, though the certificate authorizing it stands.

validity.recommendation: distinct component, not a duplicate -- no merge with P0147
validity.researcher_notes: P6534 (Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Pipeline, ~62.5 mi/32-in) is a component of the same FERC application and docket (CP17-178-000, 171 FERC P 61,134, 2020-05-21) as P0147 (Alaska LNG Mainline, ~806.9 mi/42-in) but is a PHYSICALLY SEPARATE line, correctly its own GEM row. Independently verified against the FERC order's own facility list, which authorizes THREE distinct facilities in one docket: (1) the Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Line, 62.5 mi/32-in, Point Thomson Unit to Prudhoe Bay Treatment Plant -- this row; (2) the Mainline Pipeline, 806.9 mi/42-in, Prudhoe Bay Treatment Plant to the Kenai Peninsula liquefaction facility -- P0147; (3) the Prudhoe Bay Unit Gas Transmission Line, 1.0 mi/60-in -- no apparent GEM row (already flagged by P0147's own shard; not repeated as a new finding here). AGDC's PTTL application and Resource Report No. 1 both independently corroborate the Point Thomson line's own 62.5-mi/32-in/865-MMSCF-D-avg/920-MMSCF-D-peak/1,150-psig specification, distinct from the Mainline's figures (2,075 psig MAOP, per RR1) recorded on P0147. No double-counting: P0147's 806.9/807 mi is Mainline-only and does not include this line's length.
